narrative:
The system has assessed your academic profile and calculated a 10% probability that you will fail your final year. While this may seem like a relatively low figure, the decision threshold is set at 10%, meaning you have reached the point at which remedial courses are required. This policy exists precisely to provide support before difficulties become more serious.

Looking at what shaped this assessment, three factors stood out as most influential, and notably, all three actually worked in your favour rather than against you.

The most influential factor was your reason for choosing this school, which was its reputation. Among students not required to take remedial courses, this is a common motivation, so this characteristic did not raise concern and actually helped push your result toward passing.

The second most important factor was your history of past course failures. You have none, which is a strong positive signal and aligns perfectly with students who typically pass. This meaningfully reduced the system's concern about your performance.

The third factor was your aspiration to pursue higher education, which you confirmed. Every single student in the comparison group who is not obliged to take remedial courses shares this goal. Your ambition is therefore a reassuring indicator and also worked in your favour.

Despite these positive signals, your overall profile still reached the threshold that triggers mandatory support. This likely reflects a combination of subtler patterns across your full profile.

You should engage fully with the remedial courses offered. Given your clear ambitions and clean academic record, this is an opportunity to consolidate your strengths and ensure you finish the year successfully.
